research_notes: The eventual runtime-health monitor can use classified probe outcomes rather than raw errors to avoid overreacting to irrelevant tool anomalies.
A rolling clean-close rate near the cap is a more useful health signal than total error count.
Wake-success rate should be monitored separately because scheduler/provider issues can degrade relay continuity without changing runtime survival.
Checkpoint-loss rate is another separate critical metric.
This decomposition supports targeted rollback or recovery rather than one global failure flag.
Current Phase A is collecting the runtime component first.
